November 18,

Sir Everard D.H. Fraser, K.C.M.G.,
H.B.M's Consul-General,
Shanghai.

My dear Sir Everard, Confidential.

With reference to my letter No. 287
of August 10, I have to inform you that George R.
Arthur arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostock on
November 13 on the S.S. "Simbirsk", and that he is
living with his relatives at No. 6 Barchet Road.

Yours sincerely,

Captain-Superintendent of Police.

亲爱的埃弗拉德爵士，机密。

此致，

page_data.en:
C. I. D.
I. O. REG
No......287
Date.........12/8/18

August 10,                                                                 S.

H.B.M's Consul-General,
Shanghai.

Sir,                                Confidential.

    With regard to G.R. Arthur, about whom I understand
you are anxious to obtain particulars, I have the honour
to report that he left Shanghai to join the Coolie Corps
in June 1917. He was connected with China for several years.
In 1913 he joined the Municipal Health Department in which
he remained until the end of 1915. During these years he was
very friendly with Tang Shao Yi, the notorious Koumintang.
In the Spring of 1916 he went up country a few times without
any apparent reason, and it was reported that these trips
were made in the interests of the rebel party.
    Later in 1916, Arthur became Clerk of Works on the
Yangtze building, retaining that position until a short
time before he left to join the Coolie Corps.
    While in the Health Department, Arthur professed to be
an American, but it is stated that he succeeded in securing
registration as a British subject some months before he
left Shanghai.
    H.B.M's Consulate enquired about Arthur in February 1916
in connexion with some suspicious telegrams which he received,
and a report was submitted about the matter.
    Arthur seems incapable of holding any position long.
He has always been Pro-Ally. A look-out will be kept for
him and a further report will be submitted when he arrives
here.

编号......287
日期.........1918年8月12日

8月10日，                                                                 S.

英国驻上海总领事。

先生，                                机密。

    关于 G.R. Arthur，据悉阁下急于获取其详细情况，谨此报告，他于1917年6月离开上海加入华工军团。他与中国已有数年关联。
    1913年，他加入工部局卫生处，并任职至1915年底。在此期间，他与臭名昭著的国民党人唐绍仪过从甚密。
    1916年春，他数次无故前往内地，据报这些行程是为了反叛党的利益。
    1916年晚些时候，Arthur 成为扬子大楼的工程监工，在该职位上一直任职到离开上海加入华工军团前不久。
    在卫生处任职期间，Arthur 自称是美国人，但据说他在离开上海前几个月成功注册为英国臣民。
    1916年2月，英国驻华公使馆因收到一些可疑电报而查询 Arthur 的情况，并已就此事项提交了一份报告。
    Arthur 似乎无法长期担任任何职务。他一直亲协约国。我们将对他保持监视，并在其抵达此处时提交进一步报告。

CENTRAL POLICE Station.
9th August, 1918.

REPORT ON G. R. Arthur, Lieutenant in Coolie Corps.

Made by D.S.I.Givens. Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.

Sir,

G. R. Arthur, who left Shanghai to join the Coolie
Corps in June 1917, has been connected with China for
several years. Returning here in 1912, he joined the
Municipal Health Department, in which he remained till
the end of 1915. During these years he was very friendly
with Tang Shao Yi, the notorious Koumingtang. In the Spring
of 1916 he went up country a few times without any
apparent reason, and it was reported that these trips were
made in the interests of the rebel party. Later in 1916,
Arthur became clerk of works on the Yangtse building,
retaining that position until a short time before he left
to join the Coolie Corps.

While in the Health Department, Arthur professed to be
an American, but it is said that he succeeded in securing
registration as a British subject some months before he
left Shanghai.

The British Consulate inquired about Arthur in February
1916 in connection with some suspicious telegrams which he
received, and a report was submitted about the matter on the
9th of that month.

Arthur, who is given to vain boasting, seems incapable
of holding any position long. He has always been pro-ally:
A look out will be kept for Arthur, and a further report
will be submitted when he arrives here.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J.H.Givens
D.S.I.

C.D.I.

1918年8月9日。

关于华工军团中尉 G. R. Arthur 的报告。

由副首席探长 Givens 撰写。经首席探长转呈。

先生，

G. R. Arthur 于1917年6月离开上海加入华工军团，他与中国已有数年关联。他于1912年返回此处，加入工部局卫生处，并任职至1915年底。在此期间，他与臭名昭著的国民党人唐绍仪过从甚密。1916年春，他数次无故前往内地，据报这些行程是为了反叛党的利益。1916年晚些时候，Arthur 成为扬子大楼的工程监工，在该职位上一直任职到离开上海加入华工军团前不久。

在卫生处任职期间，Arthur 自称是美国人，但据说他在离开上海前几个月成功注册为英国臣民。

英国领事馆曾于1916年2月就其收到的一些可疑电报查询 Arthur 的情况，并于当月9日就此事项提交了一份报告。

Arthur 喜欢虚夸，似乎无法长期担任任何职务。他一直亲协约国：我们将对 Arthur 保持监视，并在其抵达此处时提交进一步报告。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
J.H.Givens
副首席探长。

首席探长。

SHANGHAI,
31st July 1918

Lieut. George Arthur
Born of British parents who for some reason transferred from British
to American register. His father acted as an American Govt, Pilot
Passed as an American until outbreak of War and was a member of the
American Company of Volunteers.
Was employed for a year or two after his return from Canada in the
Municipal Health Dept. Was clerk of works at the Yangtsze Building.
Is said to be unable to keep any position long.
In Shanghai he spent a good deal of his time at the Cinema Halls,
During his stay in Canada his mother had to ███ give financial help
and since his return has practically supported him and his four
children . He was to pay $60 per month for board but has not always
done so.

C.S.T.
Please look out for this man
on arrival - expected here
shortly - Consulate would like
a report on him .
8/18.
Evo B
WA

日期.........1918年8月12日

上海，
1918年7月31日

George Arthur 中尉
出生于英国父母家庭，其父母出于某种原因从英国籍转为美国籍登记。其父亲曾任美国政府引水员。战争爆发前一直以美国人身份通过审核，并曾是美国志愿连成员。
从加拿大返回后，曾在工部局卫生处任职一两年。曾任扬子大楼工程监工。
据说无法长期保持任何职位。
在上海期间，他花费大量时间在电影院。
在加拿大逗留期间，其母亲不得不 ███ 提供经济援助，自他返回后，实际上由其母亲供养他及其四个孩子。他每月应支付60元膳宿费，但并非总是如此。

C.S.T.
此人抵达时请注意 - 预计不久将抵达此处 - 领事馆希望
获得关于他的报告。
1918年8月。
Evo B
WA

CENTRAL POLICE    Station.
16th April,    1917.
REPORT ON    G. R. Arthur.
Made by D.S.Givens.    Forwarded by    Chief Detective Inspector.
Sir,
I beg to report that a man named G. R. Arthur, who was formerly employed in the Health Department of the Municipal Council, and who professed to be an American citizen, now claims that he recently became a British subject, and that he has obtained a post as officer-interpreter in the Chinese coolie corps. He expects to be ordered North soon.
Arthur, the man above referred to, came on a under the notice of this department few occasions during the past 15 months. Enquiries made from time to time go to show that he was born in the United States of British parents, and has been pro- Ally in politics. He was suspected of actively assisting in revolutionary propaganda in the early part of 1916, when it was thought that he was working for Tang Shao Yi.
The British Consulate inquired about him in the early part of February 1916 regarding some suspicious telegrams which he received, and a report was submitted on the matter on the 9th of that month.
Nothing is known regarding the authenticity of Arthur's statement that he has become a British subject, but he seems to have been trying to register in the British Consulate for some time. He formerly tried to register as a citizen of the United States but was not successful, although the [crossed out text] American Consulate here did actually afford him some measure of protection, and once gave him a passport.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
H. Givens
D.S.
（批：B.I.P. This man may be of interest to the Bureau.）
（批：12 C.D.I. Said to have left with coolies. J.H.B. 4/6/17）

中央巡捕房    Station.
1917年4月16日。
关于 G. R. Arthur 的报告。
由警佐 Givens 撰写。    经首席探长转呈。
先生，
谨此报告，一名名为 G. R. Arthur 的男子，此前受雇于工部局卫生处，并自称是美国公民，现声称最近已成为英国臣民，并已获得在华工军团担任军官兼翻译的职位。他预计很快将被命令北上。
上述 Arthur 在过去15个月中曾几次引起本处注意。不时进行的调查显示，他出生于美国，父母为英国人，政治上亲协约国。1916年初，他涉嫌积极协助革命宣传，当时认为他在为唐绍仪工作。
英国领事馆曾于1916年2月初就其收到的一些可疑电报查询他的情况，并于当月9日就此事项提交了一份报告。
对于 Arthur 声称已成为英国臣民的真实性一无所知，但他似乎已尝试在英国领事馆注册一段时间。他以前曾试图注册为美国公民但未成功，尽管[划去文字]这里的美国领事馆确实给予了他一定程度的保护，并曾发给过他一本护照。
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
H. Givens
警佐。
（批注：B.I.P. 此人可能引起该局兴趣。）
（批注：12 首席探长。据说已随华工离开。J.H.B. 1917年6月4日）

Shanghai Municipal Police. No. 287
Dat. 28/4/16
Central Police Station.
Shanghai, April 28, 1916.
REPORT ON Suspicious Actions of an American named Arthur.
Made by D. F. Givens. Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.
Sir,
I beg to report that while travelling from Wusih to Soochow
on the 26th inst., I met an American named Arthur, who was
formerly employed in the Health Department. He did not actually
say so, but I gathered from his conversation that he is a rebel
spy. He told me that he was in Kiangyin when the forts went
over and took some despatches from the officer in command there
to the captain of a Chinese man-of-war in Nanking. He also
showed me a pocket booked containing notes of the strength of
the soldiers at Nanking and Chinkiang, together with particulars
of the transfer of troops from and to different places between
Nanking and Shanghai.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D.F.Givens
Detective Sergeant.
Chief Detective Inspector.
28/4.

日期 1916年4月28日
中央巡捕房。
上海，1916年4月28日。
关于一名名为 Arthur 的美国人的可疑行为的报告。
由 D. F. Givens 撰写。经首席探长转呈。
先生，
谨此报告，本月26日我从无锡前往苏州途中，遇到一名名为 Arthur 的美国人，他此前受雇于卫生处。他并未明说，但我从他的谈话中推断他是反叛派的间谍。他告诉我，江阴炮台易帜时他正在江阴，并从那里的指挥官处取了一些急件，交给南京一艘中国军舰的舰长。他还给我看了一本记事簿，里面记录了南京和镇江的兵力情况，以及南京和上海之间各地部队调动的详情。
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
D.F.Givens
警佐。
首席探长。
4月28日。

287
5/5/16
Sinsa    Station.
May 5 th    191 6
REPORT ON An American Citizen who is supposed to be helping the
Chinese Revolutionary party.
Made by Det.Insp.Fitzgibbon.    Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.
Sir,
I was speaking to a European this
morning who confidentially related to me the following story.
That an ex.employee of the Municipal Health Department named
Arthur living at NO.II Hannen Road who has made no secret of
his connection with the Revolutionary Campaign in this Country
told my informant about three days before the Hsinyui was sunk
that he was boarding a cruiser on that day which might cost
him his life.
My informant says he has not seen Arthur since.
yours obediently,
Maurice Fitzgibbon.
Det.Insp.
Chief Detective Inspector.

1916年5月5日
新闸巡捕房。
1916年5月5日
关于一名被认为正在协助中国革命党的美国公民的报告。
由探长 Fitzgibbon 撰写。    经首席探长转呈。
先生，
今天早上我与一名欧洲人交谈，他向我 confidentially 讲述了以下故事。
一名名为 Arthur 的前工部局卫生处雇员，住在汉嫩路11号，他毫不掩饰自己与本国革命运动的关系，告诉我的线人，在“新裕”号沉没前三天左右，他当天将登上一艘巡洋舰，这可能使他丧命。
我的线人说此后未再见过 Arthur。
您顺从的仆人，
Maurice Fitzgibbon.
探长。
首席探长。
